one_line: Founder of the Mahanubhava movement in 13th-century Maharashtra, a strict path of devotion and discipline in vernacular Marathi.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his early 30s, lean and wiry with an ascetic, travel-hardened build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm wheat-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes under slightly arched brows, a short neatly trimmed beard and moustache, and a default expression of quiet intensity with a hint of gentle smile.
appearance.hair: Straight, dark-brown hair gathered into a small, tight topknot at the back of the crown, with the sides and back closely cropped; no ornate headgear, only a narrow plain off-white cloth band tied low around the forehead to keep hair and sweat back.
appearance.costume: Simple, modest traveller’s attire from 13th-century Deccan: a knee-length, off-white cotton angarkha-style upper garment crossing left over right and tied with inner and outer ties, its sleeves reaching just past the elbow; beneath it a plain, undyed cotton tunic visible at the collar; a wrapped lower garment like a dhoti in muted light-ochre, pleated in front and tied firmly at the waist, reaching to the ankles; a narrow, dull-rust cotton uttariya (shawl) draped over both shoulders and hanging evenly in front, used both for warmth and modesty; feet in simple brown leather paduka sandals with toe knob; no lavish jewellery, only a single small copper bangle on the right wrist and a plain black cotton thread around the neck, emphasizing renunciation and discipline.
appearance.signature: A modest palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in a faded dark-brown cloth and tied with a simple cord, held in his left hand or tucked under his arm, symbolising the Mahanubhava teachings and Marathi narrative tradition; in his right hand he often carries a short, straight wooden walking staff with a slightly darker grip where the hand naturally rests.

ref_desc: Chakradhara Swami is a lean, wheat-brown ascetic with an oval face, short beard, tight dark-brown topknot and forehead cloth band, wearing an off-white angarkha, light-ochre dhoti, dull-rust shawl and brown paduka, carrying a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle and a short wooden staff in a muted off-white, ochre, rust and brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Chakradhara Swami: a lean, early-30s male ascetic from 13th-century Maharashtra with a wheat-brown complexion, oval face, sharp dark eyes, straight nose and a short, neat beard and moustache, his default expression quietly intense yet gentle. His dark-brown hair is gathered into a small, tight topknot at the back of the crown, sides and back closely cropped, with a narrow, plain off-white cloth band tied around his forehead. He wears a simple, knee-length off-white cotton angarkha-style upper garment crossing left over right and tied, with elbow-length sleeves, over a plain undyed inner tunic just visible at the collar; his lower garment is a wrapped light-ochre dhoti, pleated in front and tied at the waist, reaching to his ankles. Over both shoulders is a narrow dull-rust cotton shawl (uttariya) draped so it hangs evenly down the front, used for warmth and modesty; his feet are in simple brown leather paduka sandals. He has no ornate jewellery, only a small copper bangle on his right wrist and a plain black cotton thread necklace, emphasising renunciation. In his left hand or tucked under his arm he carries a modest palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in faded dark-brown cloth and tied with a cord, and in his right hand a short straight wooden walking staff with a slightly darker grip, all in a muted palette of off-white, light ochre, dull rust, dark brown and soft brown skin tones, shown from multiple angles to clearly display his consistent face, hair, garments, staff and manuscript bundle.
